newsitem.title: USA: State Farm sees at least $35 mln in storm losses.
newsitem.headline: State Farm sees at least $35 mln in storm losses.

text.p: State Farm, the nation's largest personal property insurer, said it expects to receive more than 10,000 claims for insured losses totaling at least $35 million from tornadoes that struck Arkansas and flooding in the Ohio Valley earlier this month.
State Farm has about 28 percent of the homeowners market in Arkansas, 20 percent in Kentucky, 22 percent in Ohio and 25.4 percent in Tennessee.
Nationwide Insurance on Friday said it expects to receive about 2,400 claims for losses of about $10.6 million from the storms.
Industrywide estimates of losses from the storms are expected later this week, according to Property Claim Services (PCS), an industry-supported organization that tracks insurance losses.
State Farm said it expects insured losses from the tornadoes in Arkansas to total about $14.1 million.
Insured losses from the flooding are expected to total about $18 million in Kentucky, about $2.4 million in Tennessee, and about $2.2 million in Ohio, State Farm said.
Overall damage estimates along the Ohio River and its tributaries ranged upward of $500 million in Kentucky, Ohio, West Virginia and Indiana. But much of that damage is uninsured.
The death toll from the floods stood at 31 on Sunday.
